      5 out of 5 stars
      Motorola Razr 60 Ultra - After One Week
      Build & Feel: The Razr 60 Ultra feels very sturdy and premium. The flip design is satisfying and stands out from regular phones. It’s comfortable in hand and easy to carry. Performance: It runs smoothly thanks to a fast processor and plenty of RAM and storage. Everyday tasks, multitasking, and even gaming work well. Software: Motorola’s software is clean and user-friendly. There are good customisation options and helpful features, though nothing overwhelming. Battery: Battery life is decent for a flip phone—enough for a full day with normal use. It’s not meant for heavy gaming or all-day streaming, but occasional games are fine. The phone gets a bit warm when charging or using the camera, but never overheats. Who Should Buy: This phone isn’t for everyone. If you want a flip phone experience with modern features, this is the best choice. For those who prefer traditional phones or need very long battery life, look elsewhere. Verdict: A stylish, sturdy flip phone with good performance and software. Great for anyone looking for something unique and fun to use.

        My First Motorola—and What a Flip! The Razr 60 Ultra Truly Surprised Me
        Reviewed in India on 5 October 2025
        Colour: PANTONE Rio RedSize: 16GB+512GB
        Verified Purchase
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.

        Motorola Razr 60 Ultra my first Motorola Phone . Initially I was very skeptical particularly about the air and hyoe around Foldable and flip genre

        With Samsung Rampant and aggressive marketing and with motorola catching up latest I zeroed in on Motorola after about 1 month of research. I got first hand review from customer who had bought this I haven't used a Samsung phone till date however I will be happy to break this jinx in future with an upgrade after 3 yrs. So after a lot of pixels and one plus this seems a apt choice

        The build quality is premium, the cover display is incredibly practical, and the performance feels snappy and fluid. The foldable screen feels refined — no creases that bother your eyes — and the phone just exudes confidence.

        Battery life has been better than expected, and the camera performance, while not top-tier flagship level, is definitely dependable for everyday shots.

        Coming from a long line of Pixels and OnePlus devices, this feels like a fresh, futuristic experience. It’s not just a phone; it’s a statement piece that combines style and substance beautifully.

        My Verdict:

        Motorola has truly matured with this one. The Razr 60 Ultra isn’t just a comeback — it’s a redefinition of what a foldable can be. If you’ve been on the fence, this is the time to flip your perspective — literally.

        My Rating: 4.7/5 — Bold, beautiful, and brilliantly balanced.

        For all my friends who would argue why not 5/5

        1. Camera: Good, but not flagship-level

        2. Battery Life: Decent, not stellar

        .3.Software Update Commitment only 3 yrs

        4. Ecosystem & Accessories it lacks dedicated ecosystem

        A near perfect filp experience.

        **⭐☆☆☆☆ (1 Star)**

        **⚠️ Buyers Beware: Foldable Screen Failed Within Warranty — No Support**

        I bought the Motorola Razr 60 from Amazon on 29 May 2025, expecting a premium experience. Instead, within the warranty period, the display developed damage **right along the fold/crease**—during normal, careful use.

        No drops. No mishandling. This is the **core feature of the phone**, and it failed.

        What’s worse? The authorized service center refused warranty coverage, leaving me with a defective device and no accountability. Now having this on hand, don't know what to do with this ₹1lakh paper weight

        👉 If a foldable phone cannot withstand regular folding, what exactly are we paying for?

        **⚠️ Key Issues:**

        * Display failure at the crease (design flaw)

        * Happened within warranty period

        * Warranty claim rejected

        * Poor after-sales support

        **💬 Final Word:**

        This is a premium-priced product with **serious durability issues and unreliable support**. Think twice before buying—you may be on your own if something goes wrong.

        It runs smoothly thanks to a fast processor and plenty of RAM and storage. Everyday tasks, multitasking, and even gaming work well.

        Software:

        Motorola’s software is clean and user-friendly. There are good customisation options and helpful features, though nothing overwhelming.

        Battery:

        Battery life is decent for a flip phone—enough for a full day with normal use. It’s not meant for heavy gaming or all-day streaming, but occasional games are fine. The phone gets a bit warm when charging or using the camera, but never overheats.

        Who Should Buy:

        This phone isn’t for everyone. If you want a flip phone experience with modern features, this is the best choice. For those who prefer traditional phones or need very long battery life, look elsewhere.

        Verdict:

        A stylish, sturdy flip phone with good performance and software. Great for anyone looking for something unique and fun to use.

      • NIRMESH PANDEY
        1 out of 5 stars
        Worst Phone Ever -Foldable part will be surely damage .Don't buy
        Reviewed in India on 7 October 2025
        Colour: PANTONE Rio RedSize: 16GB+512GB
        Verified Purchase
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
        Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

        I’m writing to express my deep disappointment with the support I received from the Motorola service center at RDC Rajnagar, Ghaziabad.

        I purchased the Moto Razr 60 Ultra for ₹1,00,000, expecting premium quality and service. However, within just 3 months, the front display of the foldable screen went completely blank. I visited the service center, and they refused to repair it under warranty, citing a minor scratch on the back panel — which clearly has no connection to the screen failure.

        When I asked about paid repair options, I was shocked to hear that the front screen replacement would cost ₹39,000 and the back panel ₹11,000 — totaling over ₹50,000. That’s half the cost of the phone!

        This experience has been extremely frustrating. I strongly advise others to reconsider buying Motorola foldable phones. The support team was unhelpful, and the repair costs are unreasonable. I regret choosing Motorola over more reliable brands like Samsung or Apple.

        A phone bought for ₹1,00,000 now has a resale value of barely ₹80,000, and the repair cost makes it the worst value for money I’ve ever experienced.

        Please take this feedback seriously and improve your customer support and warranty policies
